description: aiogram is a modern and fully asynchronous framework for Telegram Bot API written in Python using asyncio

latest_release.name: Security fixes and Testing World
latest_release.body:
This release fixes three security advisories; upgrading is recommended:
[GHSA-52j5-qrwv-2vf2](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-52j5-qrwv-2vf2) (bot token in network errors),
[GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h) (filter bypasses) and
[GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83) (webhook / undecodable updates, union validation cost).
All three were reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner.

## Security

- `CallbackData.pack()` now refuses values that would not unpack back unchanged with a self-overlapping multi-character separator (such as `"--"`), instead of letting the end of one value shift into the next field. Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-0M5J1VQ7).
  [GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h)

- `MaybeInaccessibleMessageUnion` is now discriminated by `date` (`0` means `aiogram.types.inaccessible_message.InaccessibleMessage`), so nested messages are validated once instead of once per member, which took time exponential in the nesting depth.
  Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-IOHAUKLG).
  [GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83)

- `StateFilter(Group)`, `Group()` and `"..." in Group` now match the states of a `StatesGroup` nested three or more levels deep. Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-664Y7GWN).
  [GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h)

- `Update.event_type` no longer keeps the last 128 updates alive in a process-wide cache; `aiogram.utils.mypy_hacks` is removed.
  Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-PX6H5HDK).
  [GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83)

- `and_f(...)` now passes the data returned by a filter on to the next filters, as filters registered in a row already do. Previously a later filter in `and_f` did not see it, and a negated check on that value always passed. Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-RO3G83HJ).
  [GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h)

- A filter that returns a coroutine or another awaitable instead of a result, such as a synchronous function or `lambda` that calls an async function, an `async def` wrapper around a synchronous function built with `functools.wraps`, or `functools.partial` over a `Filter` instance, now raises `TypeError` instead of passing for every update. aiogram does not await such results: declare async filters with `async def`. Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-IYO3AS6K).
  [GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-fvpw-9jw8-rj3h)

- Fixed the bot token appearing in network errors.
  `aiogram.exceptions.TelegramNetworkError` and the `aiohttp` errors raised by `Bot.download_file()` / `Bot.download()` now show the token as `<bot id>:***` in their message and traceback, and keep their type, so existing `except` clauses still catch them.
  The original exception is available as `.original` and may contain the token.
  Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-4GL80S7S).
  [GHSA-52j5-qrwv-2vf2](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-52j5-qrwv-2vf2)

- List fields of Telegram objects, including nested rich text arrays, now stop validation at the first invalid item instead of collecting one error per item, so a validation error reports only the first invalid item of a list. The minimum supported pydantic version is now 2.8.0.
  Reported by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-NM3LC5D1).
  [GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83](https://github.com/aiogram/aiogram/security/advisories/GHSA-hv98-r5fx-wc83)

- Passing filters to a Scene entry point, `on.<event>.enter(...)`, now emits a `DeprecationWar
